items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: I, uh, got to know Danny Barker and Alan Nicholas... played a few jobs with Nicholas and, uh, with Danny.

ctx.x: What about the other New Orleans musicians up there?

Well, you mean, aside from Bunk's band? Yeah. Well, I, uh, got to know Danny Barker and Alan Nicholas, uh, while I was up there more than any other, uh, of the New Orleans musicians. Uh, played a few jobs with Nicholas and, uh, with Danny. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Pops Foster.
What do you think of their approach as compared with the approach of, say, the Joyce Lewis group, or with Lone Johnson's approach?

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: This was Cuffee and Danny Barker and Kirkpatrick on piano and Groh and Steele. And did we say Bushell? Yeah. No, we didn't make it. And Bunk. And they had a very warm thing going.

ctx.x: He never wanted to fly. He always refused to fly.

I remember he was sick in the stomach when he got the plane just in...the plane just came in just in time to make the concert. And I remember, I don't recall where the concert was, probably Town Hall. Yeah, I think so. But I think...I know Lead Belly was there, and Danny Barker, and Simeon was there. I can remember Bunk coming in, and he looked pretty bad, and he said he felt pretty bad. He was sick, and he had an upset stomach on the airplane. And he didn't feel too good, and he wasn't playing too well at that…

Nicholas was in some of those things too. Yeah. I have a postcard, I think, listing that concert. I know, I think Maud, someone told me that she had to get Bunk on the plane finally, that... I don't know what she was doing in New Orleans or how they got him on the plane, but he would never take it under his own free will, except he was the only chance he could have possibly gotten there. He probably didn't want to go to the concert in the first place. He knew it was going to be bad. Yeah. In a bad group. He…
